short: English cleric and theologian who founded the Methodist movement within the Church of England.
full:
John Wesley was an ordained Anglican clergyman who, alongside his brother Charles, formed a "Holy Club" at Oxford dedicated to rigorous religious study and charitable works. Following a profound spiritual awakening in 1738, he began preaching in the open air to reach the working classes, travelling relentlessly on horseback across Britain and Ireland to deliver an estimated 40,000 sermons.

His dynamic preaching and exceptional organisational skills led to the establishment of Methodist societies, which emphasised personal salvation, methodical Bible study, and social welfare. Although Wesley insisted he was a loyal member of the Church of England, the movement's rapid growth and independent structures inevitably led to its formal separation as the Methodist Church after his death.
